title: GOOD: comment clarifies whitelist does not bypass AUTH
description: The comment at session.rs lines 189-191 explicitly states that connection_whitelisted does NOT bypass SMTP AUTH — it only bypasses anti-spam filters (DNSBL, FCrDNS, greylisting). This is security-critical documentation. The code enforces the distinction: the whitelist flag is consumed only by the greylisting bypass path, while MAIL FROM authentication is governed independently by the credential_store.is_empty() check. Without the comment, a future developer optimizing the whitelisting path might reasonably infer that a trusted peer should also skip AUTH (a common but incorrect assumption in MTA implementations). Making the security boundary explicit in-line with the flag declaration prevents that class of regression. Alternative avoided: leaving the security property implicit in the logic, which would require a reader to trace both the whitelist path and the AUTH enforcement path separately to understand that they are independent.
